The Tech Principle · strategy selection in three steps

Select. Compare. Switch.

How this works

A scenario selects a strategy. It is compared with similar, opposite, overall and best win rate strategies. You switch only if a comparison strategy is performing better. Real data from , embedded in this file; every choice uses only what was known at the decision time.

Where this comes from

This explorer is a simplified, static version of the strategy directory's Scenario & Criteria Universal Engine, the full interactive tool that ranks strategies, replays a day and follows the leaders. The screen below is that tool: forex, GBPAUD_C, Friday 9 October 2026, replayed to 14:45. It is one example, not the data in this file.

  • Return (top left): Net Return or Alt Net. Here this is the Net | Alt net switch.
  • Scenario, day, type, product: how strategies are picked (here Top Buy Sell, forex, GBPAUD_C). Here these are the asset class, product and scenario choices.
  • Replay and baseline: the day is replayed from 00:00 to a replay head (14:45); only snapshots at or before that time are used. Here this is the hour you choose.
  • Select top #1 at a time, auto-add every 15 minutes: each new leader is added to the same chart. Here this is the idea behind switching only when a better strategy appears.
  • The chart: each line is one selected strategy's cumulative net return through the day; the marked points show when it became #1. Sharp steps are large moves in the cumulative net.

What is different here: one file, no server, a fixed data time, crypto and forex kept separate, and the result shown as a plain choose, compare and switch flow.

2 · Compare with other strategies

Best similar: same product, differs in exactly one setting (family, window, take-profit or stop-loss). Best opposite: its equity moves against the selected one (correlation of five-minute changes of -0.2 or lower). Best overall: highest net on this product. Best win rate: highest share of closed positions with a positive net. Candidates must be a different strategy with a different net from the selected one (identical results are clones and are never used). If no such strategy exists the card says so. Ties go to the lowest model id.

3 · Switch, only when better

Pick what to switch to. The chart then shows what happened next; nothing after the decision time was used to choose it. Always switch: at every following hour the selection and comparison are run again, using only data up to that hour, and you move to the best strategy of the chosen type only if its net is higher than the strategy you hold; otherwise you stay. Switching is assumed free.
